status: Closed — source, guidance, regression guard, and formal backlog closure verified
area: Captain workflow / Windows UTF-8 document IO
finding: Captain workflows can still use PowerShell content commands or PowerShell-wrapped one-liners for planning Markdown/JSON inspection even though atm-dispatch guidance says Windows planning documents must be read, compared, and authored through Node.js UTF-8 helpers. This causes repeated mojibake/range/quoting failures and can make valid Traditional Chinese UTF-8 look corrupted.
expectedBehavior: When a task touches CJK planning Markdown/JSON/text, the active captain and sidecars should treat Node.js UTF-8 document IO as a hard preflight rule. PowerShell may launch node, git, or ATM CLI commands, but must not be the basis for document content IO or comparison.
evidenceOrRepro: Original 2026-07-19 reproduction is retained as historical evidence. Current guidance explicitly requires Node.js UTF-8 helpers or ATM CLI for Windows Markdown/JSON/text planning IO, forbids PowerShell content commands for authoring/comparison, and provides a copy-paste-safe stdin Node.js example. `tests/cli/atm-dispatch-windows-text-io.test.ts` passes and asserts the safe example, UTF-8 read path, and absence of node eval routes; the same rule is present in the dispatch, governance-router, and plan-authoring instruction/prompt surfaces.
followUp: Keep the Windows text-IO rule covered by the existing instruction-surface regression test. Any future dogfood finding should open a new dated backlog item rather than reopen this resolved record.
